paper.title: Blind Exploration and Exploitation of Stochastic Experts

settings.name_in_paper: Blind exploration and exploitation (BEE) of stochastic experts
unmapped: Arms are M stochastic experts giving binary opinions on a hidden uniform binary state Y(t); reward is correctness 1(X_i(t)=Y(t)) but is never observed (unsupervised/blind)
Learner observes only the opinions of consulted experts; multiple experts consulted per round (committee) and agreement with committee majority vote used as surrogate reward
Experts' opinions conditionally independent given Y(t); competences p_i > 1/2

source.label: main_lemma
source.quote: Then, the regret of a BEE algorithm that picks $I_t = \argmax_{i\in[M]\setminus\comm{}}\Psi_i(t)$ ($\argmin$ for IMED) via statistics for UCB1, eq. \eqref{ucb1stat}, KL-UCB, eq. \eqref{klstat}, or IMED, eq. \eqref{imed_stat}, is bounded by: \tilde{R}_{T}\leq C\frac{ \Phi}{2p_{\comm{}}-1}, where the constant $C=10$ for UCB1, $C=\nicefrac{1}{2}$ for KL-UCB and IMED.

results.notes: Paper's regret is normalized by T; expression multiplied by T (Phi = log T/T sum 1/Delta_i). Derived as corollary of prior results; derivation is informal. K = M experts.
